focus: Dallas electricians MVP synthetic vs imported scaffold contract comparison

checks.description: All datasets keep the shared normalized MVP files.
Imported datasets include source lineage rows while the synthetic scaffold does not require them.
Imported datasets include optional rule_documents.jsonl while the synthetic scaffold can stay minimal.
Every scaffold emits at least one permit-inspection sequence for downstream task generation.
Every scaffold emits pattern slices for the pattern-extraction eval family.
Every eval scaffold exposes the same four Dallas task families.
Every eval scaffold keeps pattern extraction isolated in test, with one test row per pattern slice.
Reviewed label rows keep one shared field contract across synthetic and imported scaffolds.
The latest imported sample moves recurring pattern slices beyond one-off support.
The latest imported sample has repeated permit support for every current inspection result state.
The latest imported sample has repeated support for the main normalized failure reasons.
The latest imported sample has repeated support for the key reviewed next-action groups.
Imported samples widen the scaffold monotonically for permits, inspections, tasks, and source lineage.

intentional_differences: Imported scaffolds add source lineage through source_records.jsonl while the synthetic sample stays minimal.
Imported scaffolds now also add optional Dallas rule-document context through rule_documents.jsonl while the synthetic sample stays minimal.
Normalized row counts, eval task totals, and reviewed label totals grow across imported samples as the raw CSV fixtures widen.
Inspection result vocabulary broadens in imported v2 to include cancelled, not_ready, and unknown without changing downstream task families or split shapes.
next_gap: All current latest-import result states, failure reasons, pattern slices, and expected next-action groups have repeated support; keep the action queue and coverage report current as real Dallas import records widen.
